extracted.intended_audience: general readers, comedy-podcast listeners, and people researching or producing improv/comedy podcasts
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive overview of the Comedy Bang! Bang! improvisational comedy podcast: its recurring structure, segments, recurring-character practice, production/distribution model, and audience-participation elements. Useful as a template for the show's format and production choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed genres: Comedy, comedy music, absurdism, improv, entertainment, talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for style and comedic approach: absurdist and improvisational elements are central to the show's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes range widely in runtime; the format accommodates both short and extremely long episodes, implying flexibility in segment planning and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release frequency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A weekly publishing cadence; production schedules and backlog management should support consistent weekly releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode opening (theme song)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each episode begins with a theme song performed by Reggie Watts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recognizable opening theme provides show branding and sets tone; using a recurring performer/theme can build listener familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listener-submitted catchphrase
rubrics_metrics.description: After the theme song the host reads a listener-submitted catchphrase (traditionally under the pretense that one will eventually replace the show's original catchphrase, 'What's up, hot dog?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporates audience participation into the opening; establishes a tradition and recurring ritual that engages listeners and creates continuity across episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrity guest interview as core segment
rubrics_metrics.description: The host typically interviews a celebrity guest as the main interview portion of the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are a primary anchor for each episode; booking notable guests supports audience interest and can be paired with improv segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character entry after ad breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: After each ad break a comedian playing a character enters the show, either as an invited guest or an intruder on the recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structuring ad breaks to lead into character-driven material creates recurring beats; characters can be used to inject energy and unpredictability post-ad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvisation-driven conversation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvisation is central: hosts and guests should be prepared to riff, react, and build scenes spontaneously rather than rely on tightly scripted dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring characters and long-running story arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters can recur over multiple episodes, forming long-running story arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing recurring characters and arcs rewards long-term listeners and enables serialized comedic payoff across episodes and seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plug Bag promotional segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Near the end of each episode the host will 'open up the Plug Bag', allowing the guests to promote their projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A designated closing promotion segment centralizes guest plugs and creates a predictable endpoint; can be paired with unique musical/production elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listener-submitted plug themes and remixes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plug Bag feature has a different listener-submitted theme song each week, as well as a different listener-submitted remix of an annually-improvised Ben Schwartz song.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly invites listener contributions to show elements (theme songs, remixes), reinforcing engagement and community-created content that can be reused in future episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improv-style games and recurring bits
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier years (and many episodes) are characterised by improv-style games, including 'Would You Rather?', 'Riddle Me This', 'Freestyle Rap Battle', and other segment formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly used game formats provide structural anchors for improvisation and recurring humor; keep a library of games/bit formats for ease of episode construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest-originated features
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, guests present their own recurring features on the show (examples: 'Harris' Foam/Phone Corner', 'New No-Nos', 'The Solo Bolo Olympic Song Challenge').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing guests to bring or originate segments can introduce variety and create new recurring bits that become part of the show's canon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live stage recordings and premium releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy Bang! Bang! has been recorded live on stage at theatres around the world; these recordings were (and are) offered to premium subscribers on various platforms (Howl app, Stitcher Premium, Comedy Bang Bang World).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live shows extend the brand, provide different audience dynamics, and can be monetized as premium content; plan production logistics and post-production for live episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription/archival platform strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2021 the creators launched Comedy Bang Bang World, a subscription service offering ad-free back episodes, exclusive Discord access, live performances, and new spin-off shows (CBB Presents rotating feed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated platform can house archives, monetize back catalog, offer community features, and incubate spin-offs hosted by recurring characters and contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotating feed of spin-offs (CBB Presents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rotating feed of 'CBB Presents', where comedy friends and recurring CBB characters host their own spin-off podcasts, has included numerous mini-shows and specials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the main show as an incubator for character- or host-led spin-offs; rotate content to keep the subscription offering fresh and leverage existing audience loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show branding via recurring musical elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening and closing themes (e.g., Reggie Watts opening; 'Closing Up the Plugbag' closing theme performed/recorded by various artists) and annual musical traditions contribute to the show's brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurring musical motifs and yearly traditions (e.g., annually-recorded theme remixes) strengthen identity and give fans collectible/anticipatory moments.
